Subject: Quick recap + next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated / noisy neighbor concerns)

Alex / Casey — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align on deployment mode.

Summary of what I heard:
- Production workload: real-time customer-facing chat and classified document summarization (~120M tokens/month today, expected 3x growth).
- Latency target: p95 generation latency target around 150-200ms for key UI paths.
- Quality: prefer to use curated open models; acceptable to use quantized variants if latency/cost improves without regressing quality.
- Main concern: noisy neighbor behavior in shared pools causing latency spikes at peak; want clear isolation characteristics and SLOs.
- Compliance: FinPay needs audit logs and some network isolation — exploring Dedicated vs Private VPC.

Our recommendation (initial):
- Short term: run a 2-week dedicated capacity pilot to validate p95 SLOs and isolation under your traffic pattern. Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools, predictable queuing, and targeted autoscaling.
- Medium term: evaluate Private VPC if you require VPC ingress controls or on-prem for regulated data.

Requested items from your side:
1) Can you share a 24-72h sample of traffic (RPS, average tokens/request, peak windows) or a simple throughput spreadsheet?
2) Which SLOs matter most (p95 vs p99, or tail latency)? You mentioned p95; let me know if p99 is a hard constraint.
3) Any procurement timing or legal requirements we should be aware of for a pilot?

Next steps I propose:
- I'll send a short pilot plan and a Dedicated overview (attached).
- If you're good, we'll schedule a 30-min kickoff with infra (Marissa) to size the pilot and validate isolation tests.

Attaching: redwood-dedicated-overview.pdf (high-level)

Thanks — Priyom

Thanks for the clear recap, Priyom — this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying questions before we loop infra in: 

1) Noisy neighbor: can you quantify the isolation guarantees for Dedicated vs Shared? In particular, under peak load from other tenants on Shared, what magnitude of p95/p99 degradation should we expect?

2) SLOs: We do care about tail latency — p95 is our primary target, but p99 spikes are also customer-impacting. If a shared pool can hit p95 normally but has p99 spikes during noisy neighbor events, that may be unacceptable for our SLAs.

3) Cost / sizing: do you have a simple guidance table (e.g., requests/sec -> recommended instance type / expected cost) so I can start budgeting?

4) Compliance: FinPay will likely require audit logs and per-tenant tracing — is that available with Dedicated or only with Private?

If you can send answers to 1-4 and the pilot plan, we can review and try to get procurement moving.

Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finpay.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated / noisy neighbor concerns)

Hi Alex — looping in with technical details to address your questions. Short answers up-front, followed by notes you can use for procurement.

1) Noisy neighbor isolation (Shared vs Dedicated):
- Shared: tenants share the same GPU pools and scheduling queues. We use continuous batching and priority scheduling to optimize throughput, but under extreme load from other tenants you can see tail latency increases. In our benchmarks, typical p95 on Shared for API workloads is 120-250ms depending on model/sequence length; worst-case p99 tail spikes have occurred (rare) during cross-tenant peak events.
- Dedicated: fully isolated GPU pools provisioned for your tenancy. Scheduler and KV cache are tenant-scoped, and we reserve memory and GPU cycles to reduce cross-tenant interference. In our internal SLAs for Dedicated pilots, we target p95 stability within +/-10% of baseline under simulated neighbor load and significantly reduced p99 spikes versus Shared.

2) SLOs and measurement:
- We recommend scoping your SLOs as p95 < 200ms and p99 < 800ms for user-facing paths as a first pass. For tighter p99 needs we can run pre-pilot stress tests and adjust sizing.
- Audit logs / tracing: Dedicated supports detailed request-level logs, token-level costs, and trace IDs that can be exported to your SIEM. Private VPC adds customer-controlled networking and additional isolation for compliance-heavy customers.

3) Cost / sizing (very high level):
- Small pilot (sims to ~5-10 RPS, burst to 20 RPS): 1-2 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs - est $Xk/month (we will give exact numbers after we see your sample traffic).
- Production baseline (depending on avg tokens/request): 4-8 GPUs for medium workloads.
- We'll provide a detailed spreadsheet after we get your throughput sample.

4) Procurement notes:
- Pilot can be done under a short-term credit arrangement; procurement often signs a 30-60 day MSA addendum.
- We can provide SOC2 evidence and internal audit logs as part of the pilot.

Attachments and links: https://redwood.ai/docs/dedicated (public spec) - contains Dedicated feature matrix and SLO language you can reuse in your procurement. I'll also share an internal trial checklist after we scope your traffic.

If you're ok, Priyom and I can run a 30-min sizing call tomorrow to agree the exact pilot size and test plan.

Thanks — Marissa

--
